clue.text: Friend, old countertenor, comes from a city in California

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a countertenor sings in the alto range

explanation.surface: A friend who once sang countertenor turns out to hail from a Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Palo Alto is a city in Silicon Valley, home of Stanford University, in California.

clue.text: Colonialist entertaining scholar and author

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within one's home, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: William Penn founded the colony of Pennsylvania
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A colonial settler hosts an academic writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A penman is a writer, someone who writes for a living, so an author.

clue.text: Large body of soldiers, say, described by hero

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw it round something, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a lion is a brave person, a hero
e.g. means 'for example', which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A hero tells of a large army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described' is used in the geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit of several thousand troops, a large military body.

clue.text: Almost lost Asian ruler in Russian city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: astray means lost
a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

explanation.surface: A wandering Asian ruler ends up in a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a city on the Volga delta in southern Russia.

clue.text: Boring person studies children's writer

blocks.note: to train is to study or practise
Beatrix Potter wrote Peter Rabbit

explanation.surface: A dull person reads up on an author for children.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a trainspotter is the stock image of a dull hobbyist.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter collects locomotive numbers, a hobby used in Britain as shorthand for someone tedious.

clue.text: Unpretentious representative inhabiting isle abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters of isle are scattered
something inhabiting a place lives inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the four letters of isle rearranged, to be split around the insert
MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A modest politician lives on an island overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: MP goes inside the rearranged ISLE, giving SI-MP-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something simple is plain and lacks show, which is what unpretentious describes.

clue.text: Leaders of industry deny accident harmed our state

indicators.note: leaders come at the front, so the opening letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Captains of industry deny that an accident hurt their state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is the last word in the run of initials, so the definition is just 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty constituent states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Greek god mysteriously poisoned

indicators.note: something done mysteriously happens in an unexplained way, so the letters are rearranged unpredictably

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek deity has died from unexplained poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon was the Olympian deity of the sea in Greek mythology.

clue.text: One male brought in possessions for valuation

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so these letters go within the other word

blocks.note: a person's estate is all their possessions
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man is called in to value someone's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate judgement of value or cost, a valuation.

clue.text: Late drink may make bad thing better

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the following word's letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the letters of thing rearranged
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Advice that a drink before bed can make a bad situation improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective but is the verb, as in capping someone's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed, at the end of the evening.

clue.text: Dog, good thing to have following onset of burglaries

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of burglaries
an asset is a useful or valuable thing

explanation.surface: A dog is a handy thing to own once burglaries begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the good thing after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound breed with long ears, used for scent tracking.

clue.text: Tossed confetti at us in opera

indicators.note: things tossed are thrown about, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wedding confetti is thrown at the audience during an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Così fan tutte is a comic opera by Mozart, first performed in 1790.

clue.text: A second artist brought back bouquet

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the whole string is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist returns a bouquet a moment later.
explanation.walkthrough: A-MO-RA is reversed as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic smell, which is an aroma.

clue.text: Go on, smile, having broken down newly-coined word

indicators.note: something that has broken down has fallen apart, so the fodder's letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to smile after a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a freshly invented term or expression not yet in established use.

clue.text: At which one may have been punished if stealing mail

definitions.text: At which one may have been punished
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a place, standing for the noun

blocks.note: to whip is slang for to steal
post is mail

explanation.surface: Someone caught stealing letters might once have been flogged for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Whip is informal British for steal, as in 'someone's whipped my bike'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping post was a public post to which offenders were tied to be flogged.

clue.text: Novelist suppressing joke - it's fruity

definitions.note: read as 'it is a fruit', a noun

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down and keeps it in, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Graham Greene, English novelist
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A writer holds back a joke as being a bit fruity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests risqué humour, but the definition is a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a sweet green variety of plum, a fruit.

clue.text: Rigorous appraisal of a trial involving police branch

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so the trial wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is a branch of British police
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A detective department's trial gets a thorough review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police branch' points to Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, a stock crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive trial of worth, from testing gold with acid.

clue.text: A racket, rising commotion in slaughterhouse

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a bat or racket, used to hit a ball
a riot is a commotion

explanation.surface: A noisy uproar builds up in a slaughterhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like noise, beside commotion, but it is the sports implement.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a building where animals are killed for meat, a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: George Hepplewhite's PM?

blocks.note: surface reading: a Prime Minister, who forms a government team
setter's reading: Hepplewhite was an 18th-century furniture craftsman, so his trade is meant

explanation.walkthrough: A Prime Minister picks the ministers of government, so a PM forms a cabinet; Hepplewhite made the wooden furniture kind.
explanation.definitionFit: George Hepplewhite was a celebrated English craftsman of fine wooden furniture such as cupboards and chairs.

clue.text: Complain about onset of pig flu

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so just the first letter is taken
about means around, so the complaint wraps round the selected letter

blocks.note: to gripe is to complain
the first letter of pig

explanation.surface: Someone moans about the start of a swine flu outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Grippe is an old word, borrowed from French, for influenza.

clue.text: Motto on one side of court

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
each half of a tennis court is an end

explanation.surface: A motto is inscribed on one side of a court building.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's field is split into the off side and the on (or leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is an inscription such as a motto on a coin, medal or coat of arms.

clue.text: Discourage fellow cleaner

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage
a gent is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put off a man who cleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person but is the substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a chemical product used for washing and removing dirt.

clue.text: Put up beams in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Lighting beams are put up in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to put it up or lift it to a higher position.

clue.text: Bottle-neck?

blocks.note: first meaning: courage, British slang
second meaning: cheek or audacity, British slang

explanation.walkthrough: Joined by a hyphen it looks like a traffic bottleneck. In British slang 'bottle' is courage and 'neck' is cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve covers both courage to act and the impudence to act brazenly, matching both slang words.

clue.text: Sexy Italian breaking heart? Just the reverse

blocks.note: the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: A seductive Italian goes about breaking hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: IT breaks into CORE to give C-IT-ORE, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic means arousing sexual desire, which is what sexy describes.

clue.text: Seek a tip cooking what's often served with chips?

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking tip about a classic pub dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips here are British chips, thick fried potato strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak pie with chips is a staple of British pubs and chip shops.

clue.text: Sailor needing to achieve objective

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
to get is to obtain or achieve

explanation.surface: A seaman needs to reach a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is a goal one aims at, an objective.

clue.text: Mother may go after this clergyman

blocks.note: surface reading: a mother chasing after someone
setter's reading: the word is one that can come before Mother in a nun's title

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go after' means follow in a phrase: the head of a convent is the Reverend Mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title and informal name for a member of the clergy, a priest or minister.
